answer: A place I love to walk is a tree-lined avenue in the park near my home, which runs along one side of the park beneath tall rain trees and a few old mango trees. It is only about ten minutes from our flat, so it is very easy to fit into my day. I try to go there most evenings after work, and on Friday mornings I sometimes go early, before the heat builds up. Usually I go alone, but occasionally I go with a friend, and now that my father has retired he sometimes joins me, which has become a nice chance for us to talk. What makes it perfect for walking is the shade from the mature trees and the wide, well-kept paths. It is far enough from the main roads that the noise fades away, leaving a wonderfully calm atmosphere. I find that walking there is not just good exercise but also genuinely [[meditative]]; it is when I do some of my best thinking. The changing light in the evening, as the sun filters through the leaves, makes the whole place feel [[serene]]. Sometimes I listen to music or a podcast, and other times I simply enjoy the sound of birds settling down for the night. When I walk with my father, he tells me how the town looked when he was young, which I find fascinating. Honestly, this simple daily walk has become one of the most [[rejuvenating]] parts of my routine. It clears my head, [[lifts my spirits]] and gives me a small [[pocket of calm]] in an otherwise busy day.

followUps.q: Do you think walking is a good form of exercise?
followUps.answer: Yes, it is probably the most underrated one. It is free, anyone can do it and it is gentle on the body, yet it still keeps you fit, especially if you walk briskly every day.
Quite a lot, particularly in the early morning and the evening. You see older people walking for their health, families strolling with children and a few serious joggers who overtake everyone.
